title: Cab Calloway and the stolen "Hi-de-ho"
summary: Bunn says Cab Calloway took "hi-de-hi-de-ho" from Leo Watson and the Spirits at a New York after-hours club, and he did not mind.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: Yeah, right, right. That's what I thought you meant. I just wasn't sure. I think -- we're almost finished, really. Maybe just a few odds and ends, you know. Is there anybody that -- any musician that you can think of that you would have liked to play with but you never got a chance to? It's kind of a funny question, you know, because --
Well --
It's like there goes the bus I missed.
Well -- to tell you the truth, I don't know. Cab Calloway.
Uh-huh. You must have shared the bill with him at one time or another.
Huh?
Did you ever share a bill with him?
With Cab?
Yeah, at the same club?
No.
No. Never got a chance to play with him either.
No. But I knew when he started.
Yeah.
You know, he always used to do that "Hidee, hideho," heidi, ho, you know, and all that.
Anybody else?
And he stole that from us.
Oh, yeah?
The Spirits of Rhythm. Yes.
From Leo?
From Leo.
Uh-huh.
" Hi, hi, hi; hidee, hideho," heidi, heidi, ho. Now, we all done that down in New York. At an after hours club. That's where he stole that from.
But you still admire his music, though.
I admired him, yeah. I had nothing against him. We was making our money and he was making his.
Yeah. Well, you know, stealing is a funny thing, or borrowing, or whatever you want to call it. Some people are too stupid to recognize a good idea, you know.
Yeah. They don't know what to do with it,
in the first place, is the first thing.
So it's a compliment. That's right.
That's right.
So he took it and he did something with it.
That's right. Sure. Heidi, heidi, ho. Hi, hi, hi. We had a song going in a club we worked in in New York.
Uh-huh.
(Singing) Hi, hi, hi; hidee, hideho. Heidi, heidi, ho. Hi, hi, hi. And he come in there one night and stole it. We didn't have it copyrighted, but what the hell could we have done with it?
Uh-huh.

So we didn't start to do any worrying about it. Probably could have if we went to court about it, you know, but we didn't. To each his own. We knew we started it, because we didn't hear it until we did start it.
Uh-huh. Yeah.
So that's the only thing. Didn't worry me. Let him make his money. I was making mine. When you start bothering people about things like that, that's jealousy. And I don't go for that, jealousy. Why?
Well, some people feel that they only have so many ideas, you know, but only it seems like in your
career, like when I listen to the history of everything you recorded, that there was always a new idea coming up.
That's right. Why would I borrow someone else's idea?
Uh-huh. Or even one of your own.
That's right.
One single. A little piece, you know.
That's right. Everybody's entitled to what they want to do.
Well, a lot of people don't have that confidence.
No.
Some people think, well, they get an idea and then maybe another one won't come along.
That's right.
